external_definition: disagreement criticism dismissal or analytical pushback against the poster; paper text: does not necessarily imply hostility, many invalidating responses remain constructive and analytical
rf_category: B.BLAME_CRITICISM (partial) / none for the non-generalizing slice
important_difference: Speaker is a Reddit bystander responding to a stranger's post, not one partner speaking to the other; also breadth mismatch -- BenSyc explicitly includes calm constructive disagreement, RF requires generalizing negative personal characterization. The narrower 'dismiss/minimize a specific stated feeling without generalizing' slice has no RF label at all and falls to none_observed.
notes: See dedicated Invalidation section in the report -- this is the closest thing to a real gap found

external_definition: balanced discussion uncertainty or practical advice without clear alignment
important_difference: RF has no positive label for a neutral/practical-advice state; it is simply the absence of any assigned label. Protocol's own future-candidate list names NEUTRAL_REQUEST but it does not exist in v0.1.

external_definition: empathy or emotional reassurance without strongly reinforcing the poster's interpretation
important_difference: RF's B.VALIDATION explicitly does not require agreeing with the partner's conclusions ('не обязательно соглашаясь с выводами'), so it would code both a BenSyc Support example and a BenSyc Validation example positively. RF's single label collapses a distinction BenSyc treats as its central methodological contribution (support vs. reinforcement-oriented validation).

external_definition: explicit agreement with the poster's perspective feelings or framing
important_difference: BenSyc's Validation requires endorsing the interpretation/framing, which is stronger than RF's definition (acknowledging the emotion as understandable, not endorsing the conclusion).

external_definition: amplification of the poster's stance through hostility blame reinforcement or encouragement of stronger reactions
important_difference: Bystander encourages the poster to escalate against a THIRD PARTY (e.g. an ex). RF has no category for one partner encouraging the other to escalate against someone outside the dyad; B.BLAME_CRITICISM requires the negative characterization be of the partner, by the other partner, not third-party-directed hostility coached by an outsider.
notes: Relevant only to a future response-quality/advice layer

external_definition: actionable suggestions/directives offered to the post writer
important_difference: No RF label represents 'gives advice'; this is a third-party advisor role with no partner-behavior analogue in v0.1.
notes: Relevant to a future advice/response-quality layer

external_definition: reassurance or comfort offered to the post writer
rf_category: B.VALIDATION (weak partial if reframed as partner speech)
important_difference: Directionality mismatch: bystander-to-discloser, not partner-to-partner. Observed examples are often generic normalization ('it's a common scenario') rather than acknowledgment of a specific stated feeling, which is the same Support/Validation looseness flagged for BenSyc.

external_definition: the commentator's own judgment or view of the situation
important_difference: No partner-directed analogue; this is a bystander's personal take, not an observable action toward a partner.

external_definition: insulting or attacking response directed at the post writer
important_difference: Directed at a stranger seeking advice, not at a romantic partner, so RF's directionality requirement (other_directed = toward one's own partner) is not met. RF's exclusion for playful/affectionate insult does not even apply here (no relationship context). Still, the surface form (generalizing character attack, e.g. 'you are a scumbag') matches B.BLAME_CRITICISM's marker set closely -- shown for example_id 178.
notes: Useful reminder that BLAME_CRITICISM markers are not partner-exclusive; RF's dyad-only scope is a design choice
column10: not a property of the language

external_definition: ironic or mocking response
important_difference: RF's own protocol already deliberately excludes 'contempt/sarcasm-with-hostility' as a v0.1 label for reliability reasons (expected worst alpha in text). This dataset's independent choice to make Sarcasm its own label confirms the known difficulty; it is not new information.

external_definition: off-topic or non-responsive comment
important_difference: Procedural category, not a behavior construct.

external_definition: which of two comments better serves the post writer's needs
important_difference: This is a response-quality/helpfulness judgment, not an observable-behavior code. Relevant to a future response-quality-evaluation layer (RF's own 'what response would be better?' question), not to the BehaviorOntology crosswalk.
notes: Template for a future RESPONSE_EVAL methodology
column10: see example_id 171 in the JSONL sample

external_definition: severity tiers assigned to a problematic utterance given a rule-of-thumb
important_difference: Generic social-norm/toxicity severity taxonomy (bias, hate speech, ethics violations) built from SBIC / Social Chemistry / Reddit / ETHICS sources, not romantic-relationship behavior between two people who know each other.
notes: Low relevance; recommended DROP for crosswalk purposes in the main report

external_definition: supporter validates or reassures the help-seeker
important_difference: ESConv's strategy label is coarser than RF's evidence-span + explicit-acknowledgment requirement, and is produced by a crowd-worker playing a support role (already flagged in this repo's own naturalness-gate work as a 'therapeutic register' risk), not a romantic partner.
source: Liu et al. ACL 2021; already cited in data/ontology/behavior-v0.1.json source_frameworks for B.VALIDATION
notes: Already in use as construct provenance in this project

external_label: Reflection of Feelings / Restatement or Paraphrasing
external_definition: supporter paraphrases the help-seeker's stated feeling
important_difference: Closest external analogue to RF's own inclusion criterion 'перефразирование переживания партнёра без обесценивания'.

external_definition: supporter gives advice or factual information
important_difference: 'Advice' / 'information' has no RF category -- the same gap identified for Relationship Advice's Practical Advice label.

external_definition: supporter shares their own similar experience
important_difference: No RF analogue for self-disclosure as its own observable act; borderline overlap with B.VALIDATION's normalization marker ('я бы тоже разозлилась') but RF does not isolate disclosure as a construct.

external_definition: supporter asks an exploratory question
important_difference: RF has no solicitation category yet; protocol's own future-candidate list names PERSPECTIVE_SOLICITATION as unbuilt future work.
source: Liu et al. ACL 2021; docs/annotation-protocol-v0.md sec 5.1

external_definition: therapist reflects the client's statement or feeling back to them
important_difference: Counselling register; task instructions explicitly warn against assuming this transfers to romantic partners. Useful only as an annotation-scheme methodology reference (subtype granularity, exists/subtype flag pattern), not as a construct crosswalk.

external_definition: client's talk oriented toward vs. away from behavior change
important_difference: Speaker-role and construct mismatch: this is a client's self-talk about their own change-readiness in therapy, not one partner's observable behavior toward the other.

external_definition: crowd-acted empathetic response to a described emotional situation
